propers.name: Collect
propers.text:
Omnipotens sempiterne Deus, da nobis fidei, spei et caritatis augmentum: et,
ut mereamur assequi quod promittis, fac nos amare quod praecipis. Per
Dominum.

translations.caution:
A pre-1955 lay hand missal, not an approved liturgical translation and never an altar book. Its rubrics, its seasonal second and third orations, its Holy Week and its sanctoral are not those of 1962. It is carried only where a 1962 formulary is the same prayer, and nothing here may be used for recitation.

Printed p. 423 under `COLLECT. Omnipotens.` after the Introit `Respice, Domine, in testamentum tuum` of the formulary headed `XIII. SUNDAY after PENTECOST.`; `eter-nal` and `promis-est` closed up. The printed Latin cue Omnipotens. and the English petition answer the target Omnipotens sempiterne Deus, da nobis. Read again from the exact registered PDF at 200 and 400 dpi on 2026-10-01; its SHA-256 was independently checked. This is the pre-1955 lay hand-missal English witness, not a modern approved liturgical translation.
translations.source_label: The Roman Missal translated into the English language for the use of the laity, first revised edition (Philadelphia: Eugene Cummiskey, 1861)
translations.text: O Almighty and eternal God, grant us an increase of faith, hope, and charity; and, that we may deserve what thou promisest, make us love what thou commandest. Thro'.

propers.name: Secret
propers.text:
Propitiare, Domine, populo tuo, propitiare muneribus: ut, hac oblatione
placatus, et indulgentiam nobis tribuas, et postulata concedas. Per Dominum
nostrum.

translations.caution:
A pre-1955 lay hand missal, not an approved liturgical translation and never an altar book. Its rubrics, its seasonal second and third orations, its Holy Week and its sanctoral are not those of 1962. It is carried only where a 1962 formulary is the same prayer, and nothing here may be used for recitation.

Begins as the last lines of printed p. 424 (running head `XIII. SUNDAY AFTER PENTECOST.`) under `SECRET.—` with no Latin cue, after the Offertory printed `Ps. xxxv.`, and ends at the head of p. 425; both leaves were opened. `par-don` closed up. Its position after the Offertory within Sunday XIII and the clauses for appeasement, pardon and granting requests answer Propitiare, Domine, populo tuo ... indulgentiam nobis tribuas, et postulata concedas. Read again from the exact registered PDF at 200 and 400 dpi on 2026-10-01; its SHA-256 was independently checked. This is the pre-1955 lay hand-missal English witness, not a modern approved liturgical translation.
translations.source_label: The Roman Missal translated into the English language for the use of the laity, first revised edition (Philadelphia: Eugene Cummiskey, 1861)
translations.text: Be thou propitious, O Lord, to thy people: and mercifully receive their offerings: that being appeased thereby, thou mayest grant us pardon, and hear our requests. Thro'.
